reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap point in Italy tagged as a data center is most likely a mistag of a small professional-services office, not a real compute facility.

The name carries two signals. "Studio" in Italian business usage usually denotes a professional practice such as architecture, engineering, accounting, or design, and "Srl" is the ordinary limited-liability company suffix. Neither is a naming pattern used by hosting or colocation businesses. The record itself concedes the point, filing the entry as a probable mistag and noting that the firm's actual line of business could not be confirmed because search quota ran out.

For AI infrastructure this matters as a data-quality fact rather than a capacity fact. Inventories of data centers assembled from volunteered geographic data will contain points like this one, and any count of facilities, any map of where compute sits, and any estimate of regional power draw built on those counts inherits the error. A mistagged office adds a site with no megawatts behind it.

The record does not say how many similar mistags exist, and it does not establish that Studio Delta Srl has no servers. It reports zero megawatts, no operator, and no website, which is the absence of capacity information rather than a measurement of zero. The nearest airport, Parma at 19.5 miles, is the only geographic anchor given, and it says nothing about grid access or power availability.
